reviews.title: One of the better ones
reviews.text:
OK so I finally feel like I have enough time in the game to give a complete review on it.
Overall this is a pretty good game whether you’re the pay to win type or casual player.

I don’t think it’s fair for me to call this game A pay to win necessarily, but it does kind of flirt with that line in some cases. It’s more of a pay to advance quickly type of game. But that doesn’t at all mean that you can’t progress in this game without spending any money. There are about four different activities you can do in the game that earn you different currency, which can be used to purchase 5* heroes. Once you get enough of the same five star hero you can fuse it into a 6* and continue moving up in rank from there. 

Now while there are in game purchases that speed up this process tremendously, it’s still achievable by simply playing the game, just gonna take longer. And since it is an idle, your tea

reviews.title: What I was looking for
reviews.text:
I’ve been playing this game for about two months now, and I have to say I’ve been really enjoying it. I was looking for a mobile game that I could play in short bursts multiple times a day and this one really fits the bill. 

Let me start off by saying that some of the other reviews are right, it is a shameless ripoff of Idle Heroes in almost every way, but I don’t care. On the other hand, some of the other reviews are wrong, you don’t need to spend money to get above a five star character, it just takes time. If you want to spend money it’ll obviously be faster like any other mobile game. To date, I’ve spent $30 to get VIP 3 status but at that time I already had one six star character and several five star.

Overall I do enjoy it, it seems like the developers update it frequently which I like. There have been several server outages which the developer made good on by providing free gems

reviews.title: Arena needs fixing.
reviews.text:
This game is a blast to play. I have played others that are similar, but they are too ungiving when it comes to the players needs. The games have to make some REAL MONEY to keep going, & that’s a fact; but to overcharge for all the needed items is ridiculous. This game is definitely more generous with giving out needed equipment rewards. 
There is, however, a big difference within the game as far as giving Dragon Coin (gold) rewards & Dragon Coin (gold) prices charged for what players need. The gold for rewards is eked out a little at a time, whereas the gold charged for what is needed is about 10 times what is given for rewards. That is the main thing that blocks building up the heroes & needs to be greatly adjusted. When that is fixed, I’ll raise my star rating.

reviews.title: Nostalgia for Soul Calibur
reviews.text: I’ve been playing pvp video games all the way back to the Sega Dreamcast and Soul Calibur 2. This is a real throwback to the single player mode of Soul Cal 2, with the tournament style and the npcs and playable characters coming from the same list. It’s still an app game, so there are limitations compared to a computer or console game. As expected, you don’t operate your own character in the fight, but you have a lot of variability that lets you enjoy more strategy and control than I’ve encountered in apps like this. You have five types of heroes (Mage, Priest, Ranger, Warrior, Assassin) from six races (Scourge, Human, Demon, Darknight, Shadow, Light). The character design from race to race is very distinctive, and even from within a race the characters appear unique from one another. Overall, a pretty satisfying game as far as apps go for free-to play (like me) or pay-to-play, wherever

reviews.title: Great Game
reviews.text: My wife was fond of Idle Heroes, but the graphics in that game were too childish and cartoonish for my taste. I prefer the look of this game a great deal more, which is what got me to give it a try in the first place. I would not even mind if the art style was even a little more mature. I’m mentioning that other game because the two have similar play styles. This game is F2P with in-app purchases, but I find a once-a-month diamond subscription gives me a lot of options. It is completely playable without a purchase, but it will take you longer to get certain heroes. Most of the baselines heroes can be advanced to become as powerful as you need with no purchases, it just takes time. As with any of these games, you can accomplish more than you think with patience and planning and a little saving up for events.

reviews.title: Worth your minimal time investment...
reviews.text:
I started uncertain if I was going to enjoy this game and it has turned into a really pleasant experience. Once you have the routine down, it only takes about 5-10 minutes to run through your daily quests and then you leave your troops to farm on their own. 
There is a significant wall, whether it be defined as a pay wall or a time wall is entirely up to you, but it is there. 5 star hero’s will come but those 6 stars are behind that wall. 
I’ve been playing a couple of months, am about to become VIP 3, and have still not attained my first 6 star hero. But, the experience itself, if you are willing to accept the wall is still worthwhile. 
Give it a look... you might just stick around like I did. ;)

reviews.title: Mature version of idol hero’s
reviews.text:
The game is fun and I don’t have to be on all hours of the day to level up. The support is quick to respond to issues. The biggest problem is getting people to continue to be active. It only takes maybe 30 minutes a day to get through the daily list and then you have the weekly events. You can easily play this and several other games and you don’t have to spend a ton to get ahead. Just be smart and save resources. Don’t get caught up trying to race to upgrade hero’s so fast. 
One suggestion would be more guild events. Or something people can do that want to spend more time in game. Too many younger players get flustered easy and give up and leave the server.

reviews.title: Where I put my time and money
reviews.text:
I have spent the last year playing lots of random iPhone games trying to fill the hole in my heart that a lack of any console of computer affords. I play twice a day and relish the time I get to sit down and check on things. 
The game is a test of temperance in that it pays to wait for events to spend resources, but in my opinion that makes it more fun because when you finally get to shell out during an event the rewards are excellent and then you can usually push to a new tier or two on the added power of spending your hoarded tokens/cards/orbs plus the rewards for using the featured resource during the event.

Anyway, I like it a lot.

reviews.title: Good game. But hard not to spend.
reviews.text: This is the game I’ve been looking for. One where you can’t get wiped out by Chinese cheats(whether they cheat or actually spend 100K on the game is beyond me). The auto gather is great. Everyone progresses, spender or not- and when you do spend- it’s not a HUGE advantage over others unless it’s bookoo money. I’ve spent probably $300 over 2 months and still enjoy every bit of the game. The events are kind of ridiculous, because you would have to spend far greater than $1,000 to complete 2 of the 4 week long events. But rewards are decent even if you don’t complete them. Lots of strategy. Support is also quick to answer with any questions or concerns.

reviews.title: Underhanded Business Tactics
reviews.text:
This developer has a track record of releasing new stronger Light and Shadow heroes with great skills only to turn around once the initial summoning events are over and nerf these skills.

This makes it easier for them to then release normal, almost free heroes with highly incentivized summoning events whose skills will cancel out one or more of the premium heroes.  

I don’t have a problem with paying for premium content but it doesn’t make me happy when, instead of the normal course of power creep making these heroes less powerful over time, this company just goes in when it feels like it and weakens the skills that the people that actually pay to play this game paid for.  Some consider this bait and switch and some might argue that it’s not but when it has become the norm it most certainly is.

reviews.title: Great game!
reviews.text:
I’ve been playing for a couple of weeks now and I really enjoy it. Obtaining new hero's is relatively easy. With a little patience, getting 5 stars heroes is easy. The fact that the game plays for you while the app is closed is awesome. It makes leveling and getting basic mats pretty easy. 

I do have a few suggestions. It would be nice if I can click on another player to see their heroes. I would like to see their gear, gems, etc and just general set up. It would be cool if there was a story mode or some sort of story to it. There are a ton of cool heroes and it would nice to read a little into their background.

reviews.title: Great game
reviews.text: The game has enough features to keep it interesting.  Graphics are well done.  Game play is fair - I’ve managed to stay top 100 for most tournaments/arenas/other rankings as a completely free-to-play player.  In game purchases do offer some advantage, but the prices are quite high for most packages considering what you get, which is my main reason for not buying anything (poor value on purchases).  After playing every day for over two months I would definitely recommend this to the casual gamer; players looking for something they can sink hours into each day might be let down though.

reviews.title: Rip Off
reviews.text: I don’t know if I’ve ever seen a game blatantly rip off another as much as Trials of Heroes has. If you compare it to the game Idle Heroes, Trial of Heroes has copied it almost to a T. I personally have Idle Heroes and can tell you that everything Trials of Heroes is, has been stolen from Idle Heroes. Everything from the summoning system where it even copies the names and ways to obtain scrolls and the hud where everything is laid out almost identically to Idle Heroes. The ability to disassemble heroes and fuse to get better ones in an almost exact fashion as Idle Heroes, and even the daily rewards, vip, and gem system is almost the exact same. This game does not deserve anything better than a one star in my opinion because of how they obviously had to put no work in and just copy another developers hard work and creativity.

reviews.title: Really great

The devs obviously reward players more for spending money, but I haven’t felt left out as a strictly free player at all. They are still very generous with events and daily rewards which provide multiple ways to summon new characters on a daily basis and to strengthen your team of heroes. The only criticism I have and it’s a small one, is it would be great to have some way to earn VIP points, even slowly, like watching a daily advertisement or something like that.

I refuse to purchase anything in game because of the constant obnoxious pop ups to purchase in game specials. They also give you a limit of like 50 hero’s to start, which is laughable. Then each time you increase your limit, it gets even more expensive for the next time. Makes it near impossible to do any merging due to no ability to stock hero’s

reviews.title: Good time waster

At this point, you get stuck waiting for your auto battle experience to bump you up another level so that you can progress. It would be nice if there were maybe some kind of bonus applied for being logged in so it would be more lucrative to do something other than idle wait to level up.

reviews.title: Don’t waste money on gems
reviews.text: The game play occurs in a few stationary screens. You can fast-forward if you’re a VIP. DON’T BUY GEMS! If you think buying 10 toons at one time will get you better quality toons forget it! After multiple tries the highest level was a 4 star. Even after spending the dreaded 100 US dollar, I could not score a 5 star toon. 5 star toons can be generated on rare occasions from the tree. It also allows you to exchange toons of the same star value and class, using leaves as collateral in the exchange. Overall decent graphics, poor toon development, and limited screens make this a poor game. I wanted it to be great, I invested cash to see if it would make it better, but it did not.

Oh and if you have an issue, don’t expect it to get fixed or to even get a response. The “Contact Us” button hasn’t worked for weeks and they don’t respond to messages on Facebook (the only website and means of communication I could find for them). Don’t waste your money, play for free until you get bored. But there’s much better games out there with much more to do.

reviews.title: Not done better
reviews.text:
Definite pay to win. 

 This is just like other idle games but done worse. Progression is almost 0 unless you spend money. If you do be prepared to have RNG against you. After 100s of random drawled Heros i have yet to see a 5 star hero. 

Needed 7 gems to level my character. They appear normally 1 or 2 times a day. I figure I would spend some in game currency to refresh the shop. 100 refreshes later no gems. It’s like they knew what I wanted and just wanted to see me waste my in game currency. 

Save yourself some heart ache and go play any another idle hero game.

Edit: so I started to change my review as they responded to my review. This usually shows me they care about improving. However they replied to all negative comments in the exact same way making me think they probably did not read my particular criticism.

reviews.title: Meh
reviews.text:
Progression is slow, the quests that come along that last for 6 days are impossible to do most of the time unless you spend a bunch of money.   Example:  one was epic summoning of heroes and I think the top reward was for 150 epic summons

Even grinding levels and auto battle, you get very few.  In the market they come up rarely to buy.  You of course can buy 10 summons for 2200 gems. 

I am at the point where progression is slow without paying, which is something I won’t do.  Also, to get really good heroes having VIP helps, but that costs money too

Buying gems gets you VIP points, it’s the only way to get VIP 
 So, VIP level 1 costs roughly $10 for the 350 points needed.  Scrolling through the list of benefits, it does not tell you how many are needed for VIP 2, 3, etc.

reviews.title: Exceptionally Boring
reviews.text: I’ve played a lot of AFK games, and this is pretty much the most reductive one. They make no attempt at a story, just presuming you’re not here for that. The characters don’t even have their own names, just generic job titles (Summoner, Executioner etc). You’ll hit the cap on campaign pretty quickly and there is literally nothing else to do at that point. It’s obscenely hard to evolve heroes since the drop rate is nil and you need a ton of copies to 6*. Save your time and money, play something else.

reviews.title: Too Many Bugs
reviews.text:

Elite Trials is glitched and medals are not awarded in the correct amount. This is extremely frustrating since medals are the main sought after reward from this type of arena gameplay. 

Wasted a lot of gems of arena tickets...

The email attachment to the account is broken so when I tried to contact via the in game system, it did not allow me to.

The difference between 1 star and a 5 star game is not only how smooth gameplay can be, but also how efficient bug fixes can be implemented.

The game is “free.”

Cons:
Very choppy animations
Cluttered UI
TONS of microtransactions

Everything about this game feels like the developers were just checking boxes for game features.

Honestly, you’d be better off setting your money on fire than spending it on this game... at least then you’d see something visually appealing before it went up in smoke.
